newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-HERMIS TRADES OWN SHARES, MAKES PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-HERMIS TRADES OWN SHARES, MAKES PROFIT.

text.p: Hermis Bank said on Thursday that it had been buying its own shares and making a profit from the deals on the stock exchange.

"We are buying our own shares to make a profit and the good results show that we are dealing quite well," Nadiezda Novickiene, chairman of the board of Hermis, told reporters. "But it's not a big profit."
The bank said it was holding less than one percent of its shares now and that the profits it had made from selling shares were "not big," but it did not say what the figure was.
"The goal of dealing in our own shares was not to play with the price of our shares," Novickiene said.
Hermis Bank shares hit a new all-time high in early trading on Friday, jumping to 250.20 litas from 241.50 litas.
Despite posting solid financial results all year, Hermis Bank shares struggled earlier, as a new share issue and a weak market overall kept their price down.
Hermis shares hit a low in May of 174 litas.

"Obviously the bank considers that at one point its shares were undervalued," said Ivo Gueorguiev, deputy chairman of Hermis Bank. "But it's not a big part of Hermis Bank's business to speculate in our own shares."
